tasks.locator: Case Reports, Case 2, 1st to 4th paragraphs (left column)
tasks.source_read: PDF PDFs/PCP/Rainey_1975_ProlongedPsychosisThreeCases.pdf (published version, scanned copy read on rendered page images)
tasks.extracted: An 18-year-old man who took a drug sold as THC came to the emergency room after 30 more hours without sleep, hostile, suspicious, ataxic, disoriented and hearing chains; the day after admission he jumped from a third-floor window, landing uninjured; after 4 more days he became more aware and remembered nothing of the previous 2 weeks. Tests 13 days after the drug suggested a chronic schizophrenic process with residual organic impairment; a month later there was no psychosis and the impairment had improved. Three of his four friends were hospitalized and discharged within 2 to 3 days.

tasks.extracted: A 19-year-old man arrested after refusing to answer questions in court was agitated, heard voices and believed he was poisoned; in hospital he was ataxic, walked around nude and thought he was still in jail; blood pressure rose from 110/64 to 160/115 on the 16th day; on the 17th day he left, improved greatly at home without medication, could not remember what had happened, said he had taken a pill sold as methadone, and a week later showed no psychosis.

tasks.locator: Discussion, 1st paragraph (p. 1077, right column) and continuation (p. 1078, left column)
tasks.source_read: PDF PDFs/PCP/Rainey_1975_ProlongedPsychosisThreeCases.pdf (published version, scanned copy read on rendered page images)
tasks.extracted: The authors are reasonably certain the men took phencyclidine from their history of street drugs often found to contain it and from the clinical picture; no laboratory confirmation is reported. As cited from earlier literature, PCP's analgesia lasts 1 to 3 hours and its psychotomimetic effects 18 to 24 hours; prolonged reactions had been reported in 1 of 65 surgical patients (10 days) and in four people with chronic schizophrenia (more than 4 weeks). The authors do not know why their patients were ill for 2 to 4 weeks and list dose, slow metabolism, toxic metabolites, idiosyncrasy or an unmasked schizophrenic process.

tasks.extracted: The abstract says most skills would recover within about 5 h and almost all within about 7 h of inhaling the reference dose, which Table 9 does not bear out for lane weaving and information processing. tasks.source_read: PDF PDFs/Synthetic-cannabinoids/Winstock_2013_SyntheticVsNaturalGlobalSample.pdf (article in press, not the final version; in-press pages)
tasks.extracted: Anonymous online survey promoted through Mixmag, The Guardian and social media in November-December 2011; of 14,966 respondents 980 had used synthetic cannabis in the last 12 months, 79.6% male, median age 23. The authors name the self-nominating sample, self-report, unknown composition, polydrug use and recall bias as limitations.
